title: Imperialism and Colonialism: The Scramble for the World

questions.question: The Berlin Conference of 1884-85 is remembered for:
options: Fixing the rules for the partition of Africa among European powers
Banning the slave trade
Unifying Germany and Italy
Dividing China into spheres of influence
questions.rationale: Convened by Bismarck over Leopold's Congo grab, it declared that 'effective occupation' on the ground earned recognition on the map. No African representative attended; by 1914 only Ethiopia and Liberia remained independent.

questions.question: Which African power defeated a European army at the Battle of Adwa (1896), preserving its independence?
options: Ethiopia under Menelik II
Egypt under Arabi Pasha
Zululand under Cetshwayo
Sudan under the Mahdi
questions.rationale: Menelik II's Ethiopian army annihilated an Italian column at Adwa - Africa's decisive victory over a European invader, keeping Ethiopia free alongside Liberia when the Scramble ended.

questions.question: The Opium Wars resulted in:
options: Treaty ports and Hong Kong being ceded to Britain
The partition of China into formal colonies
The fall of the Meiji dynasty
China annexing Korea
questions.rationale: The wars of 1839-42 and 1856-60 forced open ports, ceded Hong Kong and imposed extraterritoriality - the model of INFORMAL empire: economic domination through concessions and gunboats without annexation.

questions.question: Lenin's 1916 analysis 'Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism' argued that:
options: Colonial expansion arose from capitalism's need for investment outlets and monopoly
Empire was purely a cultural mission
Colonies should immediately unite with the metropole
Imperialism would end once railroads were built
questions.rationale: Lenin built on Hobson (1902): surplus capital seeking returns drives the annexation of markets and raw-material sources. Whatever one thinks of the economics, it is the classic exam pairing: Hobson-Lenin on the economic causes of empire.

questions.question: A 'sphere of influence' means:
options: A state retaining nominal independence while a foreign power enjoys exclusive economic privileges
Direct settler rule over a territory
A colony ruled by a chartered company
A self-governing dominion
questions.rationale: Spheres of influence were informal imperialism - China's treaty-port system is the archetype. Colonies, protectorates and dominions are progressively different points on the control spectrum.

questions.question: The Suez Canal (1869) mattered to imperialism because it:
options: Cut the Europe-India sea voyage by thousands of kilometres
Made the Sahara arable
Eliminated the need for coal stations
Was dug by the British themselves
questions.rationale: Suez slashed the London-Bombay run by weeks, making India (and east of Suez generally) far cheaper to hold - which is exactly why Britain occupied Egypt in 1882 to guard the Canal's approaches.

questions.question: The Congo Free State (1885-1908) was:
options: The personal possession of King Leopold II of Belgium, run as a rubber-extraction regime
A Dutch trading post
A British protectorate
A League of Nations mandate
questions.rationale: Leopold ran the Congo privately; the rubber terror killed millions and provoked the first great international human-rights campaign, forcing Belgium to take over as a formal colony in 1908.

questions.question: Japan avoided being colonised and itself became an imperial power primarily because of:
options: Rapid Meiji-era industrialisation and military modernisation
European respect for its ancient culture
Its lack of natural resources
A treaty with the United States guaranteeing neutrality
questions.rationale: After Perry's 1853 ships exposed Japan's weakness, the Meiji state industrialised, conscripted and modernised with extraordinary speed - then joined the game, taking Taiwan (1895) and Korea (1910). Machines, not race, decided the era.

questions.question: The Fashoda incident (1898) was a confrontation between:
options: Britain and France in the Sudan
Britain and Germany in East Africa
France and Italy in Tunisia
Russia and Britain in Afghanistan
questions.rationale: Marchand's French expedition from the west met Kitchener's Anglo-Egyptian force after Omdurman; France backed down, conceding the Nile valley and pivoting toward the Entente Cordiale (1904).

questions.question: Which best describes the long-term borders left by colonialism?
options: Arbitrary boundaries drawn in European capitals that split or merged communities
Boundaries that followed ethnic and linguistic lines precisely
Borders redrawn by the UN in 1945
Borders that were abandoned at independence
questions.rationale: Africa's straight lines, the Durand Line splitting the Pashtuns, and Sykes-Picot's Middle East were drawn for European convenience - and became the frozen, inherited borders of post-colonial states, source of conflicts from Kashmir to Kurdistan.
